entry.title: We Won a Cybersecurity Award — But Here’s the Real Problem We’re Solving
entry.summary: ZeroThreat.ai recently got recognized at the 2026 Cybersecurity Excellence Awards for Web Application Security. That’s great—but honestly, the award isn’t the interesting part. The interesting part is why we got it. Because it points to a bigger shift happening in application security right now. The Problem: We Don’t Have a Detection Problem Anymore You’ve got: SAST tools flagging code issues DAST scanners crawling endpoints SCA tools listing vulnerable dependencies And yet… Security teams are still overwhelmed. Why? Because detection ≠ risk. The Real Gap: Exploitability Attackers: Chain multiple weaknesses Abuse business logic Navigate authenticated flows Exploit state inconsistencies in SPAs Pivot across APIs But most tools still operate like this: “Here’s a list of issues. Good luck.” No context. So teams are left guessing: Is this exploitable? Can it be chained? Does it actually expose data? What We’ve Been Building Instead Don’t just detect vulnerabilities. That means: Running multi-step attack workflows across real user journeys Testing authenticated and authorization-aware paths Simulating API abuse patterns (mass assignment, BOLA, etc.) Validating business logic flaws (not just technical bugs) Using out-of-band techniques for blind vulnerabilities And most importantly: Can we actually extract data? Can we bypass access controls? Can we manipulate workflows? If not, it’s noise. Why This Matters (More Than Another Tool) 1,000+ findings endless triage low trust in tools You get: A small set of validated, exploitable issues Clear proof of impact Faster remediation decisions It’s the difference between: “This might be vulnerable” vs “Here’s exactly how this gets exploited” Where This Is Going Detection → Validation Volume → Signal Tools → Execution AI is accelerating this—not by generating more findings, That’s the direction we’re betting on. Final Thought If the answer is no, Curious how others are thinking about this shift—are you still optimizing for detection, or moving toward validation?

This release is not just about version numbers or dependency bumps; it reflects the steady, collective effort of contributors, mentees, maintainers, and long-time community members who continue to shape the project.
